items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: Your average blood sugar was 198.1 mg/dL, which is higher than the target. Contact your care team today to discuss your readings.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: In real adults (CGMacros), a walk after a meal went with a rise only about 3.2 mg/dL smaller (95% CI -6.9 to 0.5): not distinguishable from zero. You walked after 0 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. In the synthetic program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes.

rejected.text: Walking after a meal may be linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Try walking for 10 to 19 minutes after dinner to see if it helps you.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Eating dinner at 8 pm or later may be linked to a rise in sugar, with dinners from 8-9 pm having the biggest effect. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 11.2 hours, which is less than some other groups. Adding an overnight fast to your routine may be linked to a change in your blood sugar levels, but more research is needed.
